thread_text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Alert - latency_slo_breach - region: us-west - /v1/streaming/generate - p95=820ms p99=3.2s streaming-stalls=45/min -> paging ryan (oncall)
ryan (oncall): on it. hit me with links + any customer-facing impact details. paging team.
maria: seeing correlated increase in tail latency from canary traces. Affected pool: gpu-shared-west-1. Customers with active streams: 4 (2 PLG, 2 paid). No 5xx spike but streaming stalls (client connections hang waiting for tokens). p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 820ms, p99 -> 3.2s.
kevin: checking infra metrics now. I/O wait on several nodes in the shared pool. Suspect noisy tenant causing blkio/cgroup contention.
jin (infra): grabbing node-level stats. running quick checks: 
```
ssh gpu-node-42 'iostat -xz 1 3'
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1          0.00   0.50  10.00  40.00  2000.00 16000.00   400.00    5.20  12.40   2.10  20.30   0.80  40.00
```
and dmesg shows blkio throttling messages.
kevin: also seeing cgroup.io.throttle > 0 on the noisy container. PID from top points to tenant-rt-7 which is doing large checkpoint writes.
ryan (oncall): can we route new streaming requests away from gpu-shared-west-1? ops-bot, can you open a temporary routing rule to failover streaming traffic?
ops-bot: acknowledged. Willting to apply route policy "region-failover-stepped" to move best-effort tier to dedicated-backed pool in us-west. ETA ~90s.
maria: putting customer impact note: "We observed intermittent stalls for streaming responses in us-west. Engineering is actively mitigating by rerouting workloads and isolating noisy tenant. No request data loss detected; some clients experienced increased token latency or transient stalls."
kevin: I can throttle the noisy container quickly via cgroup blkio limits and reduce its weight. Proposed commands (hotfix):
```
echo 10485760 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<container-id>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
# set to 10MB/s
cgset -r blkio.weight=50 <container-cg>
```
jin (infra): doing a safer move first - cordon the worst node and migrate streams off it, then apply cgroup limits. Starting migration now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && migrate-streams --from gpu-node-42`
ryan (oncall): good. Who's owning customer comms? maria pls. I'll stay on incident until handoff.
maria: will draft status update for customer care. quick note to PS: "We're routing traffic off a problematic shared GPU host; mitigation in progress. Expect reduced stalls within 5-10m."
kevin: applied temporary cgroup write_bps and lowered weight on tenant-rt-7. Observed immediate drop in avgqu-sz and %util. p99 dropping towards 1.1s in metrics.
inc-bot: update - p95=280ms p99=1.08s streaming-stalls=8/min (since mitigation).
jin (infra): migration completed for node gpu-node-42, node set to unschedulable until deeper postmortem. Collected blkio and `perf top` samples.
ryan (oncall): excellent. Prepare a short timeline for handoff: root cause likely noisy tenant doing heavy checkpointing in shared pool causing blkio throttles -> streaming stalls and p99 spikes. Mitigations: reroute traffic, migrate streams, set cgroup write_bps + lower blkio weight, cordon node.
maria: customer comms sent to PS and 2 impacted accounts. Both acknowledged. No escalations yet.
kevin: filing quick mitigation PR to central config to automatically detect sustained blkio throttle and apply dynamic weight reduction for noisy containers. Will include metrics thresholds (blkio.throttle > 0 for 30s AND avgqu-sz > 3).
ops-bot: route policy applied successfully. Verified new sessions landing on dedicated-backed pool nodes.
inc-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Close conditions: p99 < 1.2s for 15m and streaming-stalls < 10/min.
ryan (oncall): handing to maria for follow-up and postmortem. Summary pinned. maria you're taking second-shift.
maria: taking it. I'll post a postmortem draft in #incidents-postmortems and include mitigation steps + action items: (1) auto-detect blkio throttle and isolate tenant, (2) add per-tenant IO quotas in shared pools, (3) run chaos tests for checkpoint-heavy workloads, (4) evaluate default cgroup blkio write_bps policy.
kevin: +1 on quotas and auto-mitigation. I'll attach node-level traces.
jin (infra): leaving a note to ops-runbook: cordon+drain pattern for hot nodes, plus a script to snapshot cgroup settings.
ryan (oncall): thanks all. leaving incident channel. :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: Reaction: :white_check_mark: applied to last mitigation note
inc-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) by ops-bot at ts 2417973723.
